utterance: Hello Daniel, I'm one of the doctors here. I can see you've come in about lower back pain after lifting something on the weekend, and you're hoping for a scan. Can you tell me more about what happened and how the pain feels?
reply: I was lifting a big pot plant in the garden on Saturday and felt a twinge, then I woke up Sunday and could barely get out of bed, so it has been three days now. The pain is low down on the left side of my back and sometimes goes into my left buttock. It gets worse when I bend or get out of a chair and is worse by the evening, but it feels better when I am lying still with a heat pack. I have worked from home the last two days, mostly lying on the couch with the laptop, and I can walk around slowly.

utterance: Your examination fits with a muscle strain in the lower back from lifting, not a slipped disc or a serious nerve problem. Your leg strength, feeling, and reflexes are normal, there is no pain shooting down the leg, and I did not find signs of infection, fracture, or pressure on the nerves to the bladder and bowel. An MRI is not needed at this stage. In uncomplicated back pain like this, a scan rarely changes treatment in the first few weeks, and it can show harmless changes that cause unnecessary worry. Most people improve over one to two weeks, and nearly all are much better by six weeks.
reply: Are you sure I don't need a scan? I've been really worried this is a slipped disc, and I just want to make sure we aren't missing anything serious.

awards.label: Ibuprofen 400 mg orally three times daily with food, short course
Paracetamol as the analgesic

utterance: I understand the worry. A slipped disc usually causes pain that shoots down the leg past the knee, with tingling, numbness, or weakness. You do not have those, and the tests I did for nerve irritation were normal. What you have is a common muscle and ligament strain. A scan would not speed recovery and is not recommended in Australian guidelines for this kind of pain unless there are warning signs or it is not settling after several weeks. I have prescribed ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day with food for five days, and paracetamol two tablets up to four times a day, leaving at least four hours between doses and not more than eight tablets in a day. Do not take extra anti-inflammatories on top of the ibuprofen. You are allergic to tramadol, so we will avoid that. Please keep moving gently, walk a little each day, and avoid staying on the couch all day, because rest makes backs stiffer. Heat packs are fine. Avoid heavy lifting and twisting for now, but you do not need strict bed rest. See a physiotherapist if you would like help with movement, or if it is not easing in a week. Come back sooner, or go to emergency, if you get weakness or numbness in a leg, numbness around the groin or bottom, trouble passing urine or loss of bladder or bowel control, fever, or pain that is rapidly getting worse. If it is not clearly improving in one to two weeks, come back and we can reassess, including whether a scan is then useful. Does that plan make sense?
reply: That makes sense, even though I figured I would need an MRI to see what is going on. I will take the ibuprofen and paracetamol as you said, and I will try to walk around a bit more instead of just lying on the couch.

awards.label: What he expects from the visit
Physiotherapy referral

utterance: I have also sent a referral to a physiotherapist, which you can use if you want hands-on advice on moving safely. You can keep working from your desk with regular breaks to stand and walk. Avoid lifting heavy things like that pot plant until the pain has settled, and bend your knees if you must lift. Take the ibuprofen with food. If your stomach gets sore, you get a rash, or you have black stools, stop the ibuprofen and contact us. You are doing the right things already with the heat pack. I expect steady improvement over the next week. Any questions before we finish?
reply: Honestly, I have been reading about slipped discs and people needing surgery, which is why I was so concerned, but I feel a bit more reassured now.

awards.label: What he is worried the pain might be

utterance: Surgery is only for a small number of people with severe nerve compression that is not improving, which is not your situation. Your back should settle with time, movement, and the pain relief. You know the warning signs to watch for. Take care, and we will see you sooner if those come up, or in a couple of weeks if it is not improving.
reply: Thank you, doctor, I appreciate the clear explanation and I know what to watch out for now.

awards.label: Correct diagnosis: Acute non-specific low back pain
Can't-miss diagnosis considered: Cauda equina syndrome
